length.text: Up to about 2 m (some sources 2.5 m)

overview.text: The Montpellier Snake is a large, fast, day-active snake of the western Mediterranean, very common in Spain and Portugal. It is mildly venomous with fangs at the back of the mouth, but only a few cases of people being envenomed are known.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Sources usually give a maximum of about 2 m; some give up to 2.55 m and 2 kg. Often described as Spain's longest snake.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: The Iberian Peninsula, France and Liguria in north-western Italy, and north-western Africa (Morocco and north-western Algeria). Snakes further east, from the Balkans and Anatolia to the Middle East, are now treated as a separate species, *Malpolon insignitus*; where the two meet in eastern Morocco and Algeria is still debated.

behaviour.text: Active during the day. Like its relatives the sand snakes, it has been seen rubbing its body - both young and adults do this - a habit that may play a part in social life and breeding.

diet.text: Mainly lizards; rodents, other snakes and small birds are also eaten.

taxonomy.text: It belongs to the family Psammophiidae (sand snakes and allies).
It was first described in 1804 as *Coluber monspessulanus*, in a work by Johann Hermann published after his death; the name refers to Montpellier.
